In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the condition number of a problem is a good predictor of the number of iterations needed to solve that problem using an interior point method.

the condition number is a useful tool for understanding and predicting the behavior of convex optimization problems, but that it is not a silver bullet that can be used to predict the solution behavior of any convex optimization problem.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
condition numbers for linear convex optimization are a useful and practical tool in the analysis of the behavior and computational performance of linear convex optimization problems.
the condition number C(d), which is a measure of the difficulty of a convex optimization problem (CPd), is a good predictor of the difficulty of solving (CPd) using an interior-point method (IPM).
, in general, the condition number is a good indicator of computational behavior, but it can be improved upon by using problem-specific information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
condition numbers can be used in practice to provide a useful indicator of how well-behaved convex optimization problems are and how much computational effort will be required to solve them.
